prompt:
Use the attached ORIGINAL ASHVEIL cinder bear to preserve its exact identity, massive 340kg grizzly-like anatomy, round ears, very short broad muzzle, small dark eyes, tiny stub tail, ash-tipped charcoal/soot-brown fur and rich crisp pixel clusters. All new poses must be newly drawn. Never a wolf/dog, humanoid, extra limb or extra head. Four anatomically credible stout legs and broad clawed paws, with only natural occlusion. No armor, weapons, magic, glowing eyes, fire, gore, target, shadow, terrain or effects.

ATLAS FORMAT: a square transparent RGBA PNG with EXACTLY four rows and four columns, one complete separated bear per cell, 16 sprites. Row1 FRONT faces down toward viewer; row2 LEFT nose to left edge; row3 RIGHT nose to right edge; row4 BACK faces away toward top, rump toward viewer. Each row keeps its assigned direction for all four columns. Consistent elevated 3/4 game camera and head/body scale in every row. Each silhouette occupies only CENTRAL 60 percent of the cell and has generous true transparent gutters of at least 45 pixels in a 1024x1024 sheet. No clipping or overlaps, all paws and muzzle inside the cell. No text, labels, grid lines, checkerboard, floor or backdrop. Keep stable ground-contact projection within a row.

This is a HEAVY FOREPAW SWIPE attack sequence, four unmistakably different key poses from left to right: 1 WINDUP: three supporting paws planted, shoulders twist, one huge forepaw visibly lifted and curled back beside the chest, jaws closed; 2 STRIKE: that forepaw sweeps forward in a wide low lateral arc, claws fully visible, upper body leans into it, other forepaw and hind legs support the weight; 3 FOLLOW THROUGH: striking forepaw crosses inward in front of the chest/muzzle and descends, heavy shoulder follows; 4 RECOVERY: striking paw replants and torso returns toward a four-footed guarded stance. This is NOT walking, NOT four planted idle bears, NOT a humanoid punch, NOT standing vertically like a person. Show the actual clawed paw moving through four distinct positions in all directions. Rear-view row also has the paw visible at its side during windup/strike; it does not turn around to show the face. Preserve bear mass and consistent head size.
